description: Taking a screenshot (or alt-tabbing) while a camera pan key is held used to leave the board panning forever. Godot decides 'is this key down?' from the key events it has seen, and the key-UP goes to whatever stole focus — so Input.is_key_pressed() reported the key held for the rest of the session and Main._process kept adding pan every frame. Pressing the opposite key only cancelled it out (pan_dir.x = -1 + 1 = 0) until released, then the runaway pan resumed. This scenario proves: (1) an ordinary held-key pan still works, (2) a key whose UP never arrives really does run the camera away, (3) the focus-OUT notification clears it and the camera stops dead, (4) focus-IN alone clears it too (belt and braces for a missed focus-out), and (5) the sweep covers bare modifiers, not just camera keys — a stuck Shift silently turns clicks into box-select. propagate_notification on the root is the exact call SceneTree makes on a real OS focus change.

steps.script:
var m = tree.current_scene
m.view_offset = Vector2(-2320, -600)
m.view_zoom = 0.3
m.update_view_transform()
m.set_meta("cam_x0", m.view_offset.x)
return true

var m = tree.current_scene
return m.view_offset.x > float(m.get_meta("cam_x0")) + 50.0

var m = tree.current_scene
m.view_offset = Vector2(-2320, -600)
m.update_view_transform()
var ev = InputEventKey.new()
ev.keycode = KEY_D
ev.physical_keycode = KEY_D
ev.pressed = true
Input.parse_input_event(ev)
return true

var m = tree.current_scene
m.set_meta("cam_frozen", m.view_offset.x)
return true

var m = tree.current_scene
return is_equal_approx(m.view_offset.x, float(m.get_meta("cam_frozen")))

var ev = InputEventKey.new()
ev.keycode = KEY_D
ev.physical_keycode = KEY_D
ev.pressed = true
Input.parse_input_event(ev)
return true

var m = tree.current_scene
m.set_meta("cam_frozen2", m.view_offset.x)
return true

var m = tree.current_scene
return is_equal_approx(m.view_offset.x, float(m.get_meta("cam_frozen2")))

var ev = InputEventKey.new()
ev.keycode = KEY_SHIFT
ev.physical_keycode = KEY_SHIFT
ev.pressed = true
Input.parse_input_event(ev)
return true

var m = tree.current_scene
m.view_offset = Vector2(-2320, -600)
m.update_view_transform()
return true
